errata.orig:
The ASIdentifiers type is a SEQUENCE containing one or more forms of
autonomous system identifiers -- AS numbers (in the asnum element) or
routing domain identifiers (in the rdi element).  When the ASIdentifiers type
contains multiple forms of identifiers, the asnum
entry MUST precede the rdi entry.  AS numbers are used by BGP, and
routing domain identifiers are specified in the IDRP [RFC1142].
errata.notes:
IDRP was never defined in an RFC, only by ISO 10747.

errata.orig:
An IPv6 address is a 128-bit quantity that is written as eight
   hexadecimal numbers, each in the range 0 through ffff, separated by a
   semicolon (":"); 2001:0:200:3:0:0:0:1 is an example of an IPv6
   address.  IPv6 addresses frequently have adjacent fields whose value
   is 0.  One such group of 0 fields may be abbreviated by two
   semicolons ("::").
errata.correct:
An IPv6 address is a 128-bit quantity that is written as eight
   hexadecimal numbers, each in the range 0 through ffff, separated by a
   colon (":"); 2001:0:200:3:0:0:0:1 is an example of an IPv6 address.
   IPv6 addresses frequently have adjacent fields whose value is 0.  One
   such group of 0 fields may be abbreviated by two colons ("::").
errata.notes:
"semicolon" should be "colon"
Added reference to RFC4291.
Verifier: Forward reference to RFC4291 is inappropriate.

errata.orig:
To simplify the comparison of IP address blocks when performing
   certification path validation, a maximum IP address MUST contain at
   least one bit whose value is 1, i.e., the subsequent octets may not
   be omitted nor all zero.
errata.notes:
There are a number of different issues relative to this text that need to be addressed.

1.  This text implicitly change the rules for encoding a maximum value.  As an example the address 0.0.0.255 is encoded as 03 03 00 00 00 00 according to the rule " The BIT STRING for the maximum address results from removing all the least-significant one-bits from the maximum address."

2.  The rule in no way simplifies any comparisions of IP address blocks.  If one really wishes to simplify the comparison then one needs to change the rule for maximum addresses to remove all but the last least-signficant one-bit from the address.  However it is not clear that even this would really simplify the comparison in any significant way.

If you look at the example in 2.2.3.9 - tis is not clear how having the one bit at the top of the encoding helps make the comparisons any easier - but it satisfies the requirment that atleast one bit is a 1.  If the maximum value ws encoded as  1000 1   (0x3 0x02 0x03 0x84) - a bitwise comparision routine could make for a simplified a < b comparison (looking at only the top 5 bits of the address to be compared.)

b010 represents 176.16/12, the hex representation of 172 is ac, so it should be ac10.

The IPv6 addressPrefix in question is 2001:0:2/48, not 2001:0:2/47, as explained in the text before the example.

errata.orig:
Section 3.2.3.8:
The ASRange type is a SEQUENCE consisting of a min and a max element,
and is used to specify a range of AS identifier values.
errata.correct:
Section 3.2.3.8:
The ASRange type is a SEQUENCE consisting of a min and a max element,
and is used to specify a range of AS identifier values. The min and max
elements MUST specify two distinct AS identifiers.
errata.notes:
The introduction in section 1 stresses that the objective of the encoding rules in section 2 and section 3
is to produce unique encoding and minimal size encoding of the information.

Allowing ASRanges where the minimum value is the same as the maximum value clearly violates the
objective of specifying a canonical form (in order to produce a unique representation); however the
specification as-is doesn't forbid min & max to be the same value. The corrected text addresses this.

Note: erratum edited per https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/pkix/iZnCd58xgl1C47GSeFemAU9CF1g/

errata.orig:
In section 2.2.3.3, replace:

OLD:
        If no authorization is being granted for a particular AFI and
        optional SAFI, then there MUST NOT be an IPAddressFamily member for
        that AFI/SAFI in the IPAddrBlocks SEQUENCE.

In Section 3.2.3.3, replace:

OLD:
        If no authorization is being granted for a particular form of AS
        identifier, then there MUST NOT be a corresponding asnum/rdi member in
        the ASIdentifiers sequence.
errata.correct:
In section 2.2.3.3, replace "OLD" with:

NEW:
        In Certification Authority (CA) certificates, if no authorization is being
        granted for a particular AFI and optional SAFI, then there MUST NOT be an
        IPAddressFamily member for that AFI/SAFI in the IPAddrBlocks SEQUENCE.

In Section 2.3, insert after "Validation MUST fail when this is not the case.":

NEW:
        In end-entity (EE) certificates, an IPAddressFamily containing an
        inherit element for an AFI and optional SAFI which is not contained in
        the IP address delegation extension in the issuer's certificate MUST
        be ignored (i.e., treated as absent) for the purpose of certification
        path validation. If the aforementioned elimination process results in an
        empty IPAddrBlocks sequence, the IP address delegation extension in the
        EE certificate MUST be ignored (i.e., treated as absent) for the purpose
        of certification path validation.

In Section 3.2.3.3, replace "OLD" with:

NEW:
        In CA certificates, if no authorization is being granted for a particular
        form of AS identifier, then there MUST NOT be a corresponding asnum/rdi
        member in the ASIdentifiers sequence.

In Section 3.3, insert after "Validation MUST fail when this is not the case.":

NEW:
        In EE certificates, an ASIdentifierChoice containing an inherit
        element for an autonomous system or routing domain identifier which is
        not contained in the AS identifier delegation extension in the issuer's
        certificate MUST be ignored (i.e., treated as absent) for the purpose
        of certification path validation. If the aforementioned elimination
        process results in an empty ASIdentifiers sequence, the AS identifier
        delegation extension in the EE certificate MUST be ignored (i.e.,
        treated as absent) for the purpose of certification path validation.
errata.notes:
In the RPKI (RFC 6480), some end-entity certificates are issued for
purposes unrelated to the exact Internet number resources subordinate
to the issuer, for example, in manifest signed objects (RFC 9286). The
concept of non-explicit listings (implemented using so-called "inherit
elements") is a necessary feature because the RPKI is a distributed
database in which parent and child issue certificates asynchronously.
In the normal course of operations it is possible for a child to lose
authority for a set of IP addresses or autonomous system identifiers and
such an event by itself is not intended to cause invalidation of that
child's manifest EE certificate.

Unfortunately, the design approach of using separate extensions for
the two separate resource classes (IPs and ASes) leads to an inability
to specify 'inheritance' in a way truly agnostic to the resource class
type. This design quirk has caused problems in the field, for example:
https://github.com/openbsd/src/commit/8dc3a091e4df2d836eadc187e7234dbe2712c66a

Clarifying the path validation rules is important for modern day
global Internet routing (which depends on the RPKI). The already
deployed backwards-compatible solution is that relying parties MUST
ignore uncontained inheritance in EE certificates. The aforementioned
requirement notwithstanding, either a contained AS identifier extension,
or a contained IP address delegation extension, or both, MUST be present
in all RPKI certificates (see RFC 6487, 4.8.10 and 4.8.11).
